question: What public Bicol freshwater evidence can support candidate species and separate lakelets without treating incomplete sequences or local-name reports as a complete checklist?

datasetCounts.title: Freshwater Calanoid Copepods in Southern Luzon, Philippines

query.spatialBasis: A small search window around the approximate Lake Danao, Polangui, Albay location, used only to retrieve leads. It is not an official lake polygon or administrative boundary.
limits: The rectangular query finds georeferenced GBIF results only; it is not a locality-text search or exhaustive lake inventory.
All fish sequence rows share one coordinate (13.359, 123.574), have null coordinate uncertainty and null verbatim locality; the source labels are sample codes ending in Danao.
The public metadata does not expose exact stations, the taxonomic identification method or a physical voucher repository.

otherFreshwaterEvidence.sibaLada: Bicol University’s 2023 procurement ledger records laboratory work for an ichthyofaunal inventory and genetic fingerprinting under SIBA-LADA, but gives no results or link to these accessions.
otherFreshwaterEvidence.danaoLocalKnowledge: A 2024 proceedings abstract reports 2023 biophysical/ethnographic work and local claims of abundant sinarapan; fish names are broad vernacular groups, not a taxonomic checklist.
otherFreshwaterEvidence.buhiLakelets: HERDIN’s 2011 Alda abstract reports three stations each in Manapao and Katugday, October 2010 and January 2011 plankton/water-quality sampling, and 23 unnamed plankton species total; it is not fish evidence.
otherFreshwaterEvidence.copepods: Two 2013-05-20 Arctodiaptomus dorsalis preserved-specimen records (USTZRC-0353-0070A and USTZRC-0353-0069B) are kept separate from fish; no diet or complete plankton claim is made.

crossSourceAssessment.duplicateFeeds: All 21 INSDC/ENA records match one-to-one with 21 iBOL/BOLD rows on sample code; BOLD names are BIN IDs and provide genus context, not independent species identifications. Treat as 21 sample labels, not 42 specimens or independent surveys.
crossSourceAssessment.sinarapanEvidence: The existing IUCN 2021 assessment (assessed 2020-09-07) includes Danao Lake, Polangui, Albay in its broader range narrative. NFRDI’s 2023-2024 summary reports no true sinarapan among analyzed Danao samples but gives no waterbody-level effort or detection sensitivity. The existing Sanchez et al. 2015 paper collected presumed-sinarapan Danao tissues that did not yield an identified sequence. The local-knowledge statement in the 2024 abstract is a separate evidence class. None establishes permanent presence or absence.
crossSourceAssessment.lakeIdentity: Lake Danao, Polangui, Albay is separate from the fish-survey Lake Danao in Ormoc City, Leyte. The NFRDI Leyte paper is not included in Bicol candidate records.
crossSourceAssessment.appReadiness: Three species names are sequence-linked research candidates only. The single-date/single-coordinate data, null uncertainty/locality, unverified voucher/method, incomplete spatial query, unresolved SIBA-LADA linkage and unapproved public reuse prevent app admission. No abundance, current persistence, diet, invasive status, legal catchability, safety or geometry is inferred.

disposition.reason: The records are useful sample-level candidates, but their shared low-resolution point, missing locality/uncertainty/voucher/method details, unresolved project link, limited query scope and unapproved app reuse prevent publication.

nextAction: Continue Bicol inland-water screening across lakes, lakelets, rivers and reservoirs as separate waterbody units; seek the completed SIBA-LADA fish/genetic tables and primary checklists while continuing estuary/coastal coverage in parallel.
